Model access, keys, and requests through the configured service.
Where can I check availability and pricing?

Model introductions describe the models themselves. Availability and OneAster prices come from the configured service; local test rates are not commercial quotes. Check the model entry and console before a request.
Can I use an existing application or SDK?
The examples use a chat-completions request with a base URL, Bearer API key, model ID, and messages. Check whether your client supports those settings and the request features you need.
How can I manage my API keys?

Create a user API key in the console. Its full value is shown once at creation; keep it private and use it as the Bearer credential for API requests. Check its model permissions and expiry, and revoke unused keys.
What should I check when a request fails?
Start with the endpoint, environment variable, model ID, and request body. The documentation includes a configuration checklist and shows how to inspect an HTTP response.
When is my prompt sent to a provider?

A live model request sends its content through OneAster to the configured provider. Static code examples explain the request format; signing in does not itself submit a model request. Data handling depends on the service and provider policies.
